newsitem.title: USA: Viad Corp Q4 net shr loss vs profit.
newsitem.headline: Viad Corp Q4 net shr loss vs profit.

text.p: (All data above 000s except per share numbers)

NOTES: Q4 income from continuing operations, before one-time items and asset write-downs, was $19,098,000, or $0.21 per share, compared to 1995's fourth-quarter income of $15,910,000, or $0.18 per share.

There were 2.9 million more average common and equivalent shares outstanding than in 1995, primarily from effects of stock option exercises and other issuances related to employee benefit and dividend reinvestment plans.

Viad's Payment Services subsidiary is investing increasing amounts in tax-exempt securities. On a fully taxable equivalent basis, revenues and operating income would be higher by $6,326,000 and $4,499,000 for the 1996 and 1995 quarter, respectively, and by $21,489,000 and $16,000,000 for the 1996 and 1995 years, respectively.
In 1996, Viad reclassified expenses related to its receivables sales program from Costs of sales and services to unallocated corporate expense and other items, net.

As a result, operating income of the Airline Catering and Services segment and unallocated corporate expense each increased by $556,000 and $2,157,000 for the 1995 quarter and twelve months, respectively. Total operating income remained unchanged.

A Convention Services subsidiary had a one-time gain of $3,477,000 ($2,260,000 or $0.03 per share, after-tax) in the second quarter of 1995 due to the curtailment of certain postretirement medical benefits.

Carrying values of Premier Cruise Lines intangibles and certain other assets were written down in the third quarter of 1995, in light of current and anticipated conditions in its cruise market. At December 31, 1996, a further provision for losses was made to reflect estimated net recoverable values of PCL's assets.

On December 31, 1996, Viad sold its 26 percent interest in the Phoenix Suns National Basketball Association team for $31,500,000, resulting in a one-time gain of $30,489,000 ($19,025,000 after-tax), after deducting transaction costs and carrying amount of the investment.

On August 15, 1996, Viad completed the spin-off of its consumer products business, now conducted under the name The Dial Corporation. One-time spin-off costs and management transition expenses totaling $33,000,000 ($28,985,000 after-tax), including $18,000,000 ($13,985,000 after-tax) in the fourth quarter, have been recorded as expenses of continuing operations. In addition, $5,000,000 of such costs, without tax benefit, were allocated to the consumer products business and are classified as discontinued operations expense.
